title: The Holy Mountain
hookLine: Mount Athos, Orthodox monks praying since the tenth century
carry: the garden of the Mother of God

lines: A FINGER OF LAND IN THE SEA.
cards: Pilgrims come by boat. A long finger of land in northern Greece runs out into the sea, rising to a peak, and along its cliffs and wooded slopes stand monasteries, some of them hanging over the water.
Before dawn a wooden board is struck with a mallet, and monks walk to church in the dark, morning after morning. The Orthodox call it simply the Holy Mountain. Today, Mount Athos.

teach.b: Athos is a peninsula given over to monastic life. It belongs to Greece, but the monasteries govern much of their own life on it. Only men may visit, a rule the monks keep as part of their tradition.

teach.h: THE GARDEN OF THE MOTHER OF GOD.
teach.b: Orthodox tradition calls Athos the garden of the Mother of God, and a story says Mary herself came ashore there and blessed it.
The center of the monks' day is the long services of the church, often through the night, and between them, work and silence.
Again and again they pray a short prayer called the Jesus Prayer, asking Jesus, the Son of God, for mercy. It grows out of the Gospels.

teach.h: BE MERCIFUL TO ME A SINNER.
teach.b: In Luke, a tax collector stands at the back of the Temple, won't even lift his eyes, and says, in the Douay-Rheims, "O God, be merciful to me a sinner."
The monks of Athos have turned a cry like that into a way of breathing. Why does a Catholic lesson go there?
The Orthodox and the Catholic Church share the apostles, the sacraments, the early councils and the Fathers you've been meeting, but they've been apart a long time and are not in full communion.

Catholic teaching calls the Orthodox churches sister churches, and honors their monks' prayer as a treasure of the whole Church. Some Catholics make the journey to Athos as pilgrims, as guests of the Orthodox.
For the monks, the holy mountain is about Mary's blessing and the prayer kept there, not the rock.

how: Orthodox monks on Mount Athos keep long night services and pray the Jesus Prayer through the day; Catholics who visit come as pilgrims and guests, and Catholics pray for unity with the Orthodox churches.

games.q: you're a tax collector at the back of the Temple. what do you say?
o: list the good things you've done this week.
ask God to be merciful to you, a sinner.
games.why: in Luke he won't lift his eyes and says, O God, be merciful to me a sinner. Athos monks pray a cry like that all day.

practice: Slow your breath and picture a monk somewhere right now, standing in a dim church or walking a path above the sea, praying for the world, which includes you.
If you pray, carry the tax collector's words from Luke on your breath: O God, be merciful to me a sinner. If you don't, just keep company with them in silence.

wordCard.voice: Mount Athos. A peninsula in Greece where Orthodox monks have kept a life of prayer for a very long time, known to the Orthodox as the Holy Mountain. Today's word.
